    • hasUnequalChargeSameSignPair

      public boolean hasUnequalChargeSameSignPair()
      Returns whether the component topology contains a same-sign pair with unequal ionic charges.

      The result depends only on immutable component charge identities, not on phase composition, so it is cached after the first query and invalidated only when a component is added. Ordinary binary electrolytes use this fast path to avoid entering the higher-order electrostatic kernel.

      Returns:
      true when an unequal-charge cation-cation or anion-anion pair exists

    • setBinaryTemperatureCoefficients

      public void setBinaryTemperatureCoefficients(int i, int j, double referenceTemperature, double[] beta0Coefficients, double[] beta1Coefficients, double[] cphiCoefficients)
      Sets six-term temperature functions for a cation-anion binary tuple.

      Each coefficient array is ordered a0..a5; the function is a0 + a1(1/T-1/Tr) + a2 ln(T/Tr) + a3(T-Tr) + a4(T^2-Tr^2) + a5(1/T^2-1/Tr^2). This method defines beta0, beta1, and NeqSim Cphi as one coherent binary tuple. Use setPhreeqcBinaryTemperatureCoefficients(int, int, double, double[], double[], double[]) when the source fields are PHREEQC -B0, -B1, and -C0.

      Parameters:
      i - component index i
      j - component index j
      referenceTemperature - reference temperature in K
      beta0Coefficients - beta0 coefficients in six-term order
      beta1Coefficients - beta1 coefficients in six-term order
      cphiCoefficients - NeqSim Cphi coefficients in six-term order

    • setPhreeqcBinaryTemperatureCoefficients

      public void setPhreeqcBinaryTemperatureCoefficients(int i, int j, double referenceTemperature, double[] beta0Coefficients, double[] beta1Coefficients, double[] c0Coefficients)
      Sets PHREEQC six-term -B0, -B1, and -C0 functions.

      PHREEQC stores -C0 as the Pitzer Cphi parameter and divides it by 2*sqrt(abs(zM*zX)) inside the thermodynamic sums. NeqSim applies the same normalization to its Cphi value, so every -C0 coefficient is passed unchanged. Callers must not pre-divide or multiply PHREEQC values by the charge normalization.

      Parameters:
      i - component index i
      j - component index j
      referenceTemperature - reference temperature in K
      beta0Coefficients - PHREEQC -B0 coefficients in a0..a5 order
      beta1Coefficients - PHREEQC -B1 coefficients in a0..a5 order
      c0Coefficients - PHREEQC -C0 coefficients in a0..a5 order

    • isPhreeqcCommonIonTermsActive

      public boolean isPhreeqcCommonIonTermsActive()
      Reports whether the selected dataset uses PHREEQC's common ion-activity terms.

      The opt-in keeps the historical NeqSim Pitzer dataset numerically unchanged. Explicit PHREEQC datasets evaluate the common binary-derivative F sum over every cation-anion pair and add |z_i| * sum_c sum_a m_c m_a C0_ca/(2 sqrt(|z_c z_a|)) to each ion's natural-log activity coefficient.

      Returns:
      true for an explicitly mapped PHREEQC dataset

    • setUsePhreeqcCatalogByDefault

      public void setUsePhreeqcCatalogByDefault(boolean useCatalog)
      Configures automatic use of the bundled PHREEQC catalog.

      New Pitzer phases prefer the catalog by default. When its explicit rows do not cover the complete active topology, loading falls back to the legacy binary table; the existing mixed-topology coverage gate still rejects missing theta or psi terms. Change this policy only before parameters are first evaluated.

      Parameters:
      useCatalog - true to prefer the complete PHREEQC topology, false for legacy loading
      Throws:
      IllegalStateException - if parameter evaluation already selected a dataset

    • getPitzerParameterCoverage

      public PitzerParameterCoverage getPitzerParameterCoverage()
      Audits whether all Pitzer interactions required by the active primary-salt species are explicitly defined.

      An explicitly configured zero is treated as defined; an absent database or setter entry is reported as missing. Ions below 1.0E-8 mol/kg are excluded so numerical trace material does not change the active parameter topology.

      Returns:
      immutable deterministic parameter-coverage diagnostic

    • getPitzerReactionParameterCoverage

      public PitzerParameterCoverage getPitzerReactionParameterCoverage()
      Audits Pitzer interactions for every active ion, including acid-base species created by the reaction solver.

      Unlike getPitzerParameterCoverage(), this explicit diagnostic includes H3O+, OH-, HCO3-, and CO3--. It is intended for converged reactive states: trial compositions inside the reaction solver are not a stable parameter topology. The result is deliberately calculated on demand and does not add work to the Pitzer property kernel or to non-electrolyte models.

      Returns:
      immutable deterministic reaction-species parameter-coverage diagnostic

    • getPitzerAlpha1

      public double getPitzerAlpha1(int i, int j)
      Returns the PHREEQC default alpha1 coefficient for an opposite-sign ion pair.

      PHREEQC uses 1.4 for 2-2 pairs and 2.0 for pairs containing a monovalent ion or an ion of charge magnitude above two. Dataset-specific ALPHAS overrides are not currently exposed; qualified datasets must therefore use these defaults.

      Parameters:
      i - first ion component index
      j - second ion component index
      Returns:
      alpha1 in (kg/mol)1/2

    • getPitzerAlpha2

      public double getPitzerAlpha2(int i, int j)
      Returns the PHREEQC default alpha2 coefficient for an opposite-sign ion pair.

      PHREEQC assigns 12.0 when either ion is monovalent and also for 2-2 pairs; pairs containing no monovalent ion and not exactly 2-2 use 50.0. This is significant for CaCl2: its qualified PHREEQC B2 row is a 2-1 term with alpha2=12 and must not be discarded by a 2-2-only branch.

      Parameters:
      i - first ion component index
      j - second ion component index
      Returns:
      alpha2 in (kg/mol)1/2

    • getOsmoticCoefficientOfWaterMolality

      public double getOsmoticCoefficientOfWaterMolality()
      Get the osmotic coefficient of water on the molality scale. This is the definition used by Robinson and Stokes (1965): 
       φ = -ln(a_w) / (M_w * Σm_i)

      where:

      • a_w = water activity
      • M_w = molar mass of water (kg/mol)
      • Σm_i = sum of ion molalities (mol/kg solvent)
      Specified by:
      getOsmoticCoefficientOfWaterMolality in interface PhaseInterface
      Overrides:
      getOsmoticCoefficientOfWaterMolality in class Phase
      Returns:
      osmotic coefficient on molality scale

    • getOsmoticCoefficient

      public double getOsmoticCoefficient(int waterComponentNumber)
      getOsmoticCoefficient.

      Calculates the osmotic coefficient using the Robinson & Stokes (1965) definition on the molality scale. The formula used is mathematically equivalent to: 

       φ = -ln(a_w) / (M_w * Σm_i)

      but is expressed in terms of mole fractions for computational convenience: 

       φ = -x_w * ln(a_w) / Σx_i

      where a_w is water activity, x_w is water mole fraction, and Σx_i is sum of ion mole fractions.

      Specified by:
      getOsmoticCoefficient in interface PhaseInterface
      Overrides:
      getOsmoticCoefficient in class Phase
      Parameters:
      waterComponentNumber - a int
      Returns:
      a double

    • getDensity

      public double getDensity()
      Get density of a phase note: does not use Peneloux volume correction.

      note: at the moment return density of water (997 kg/m3)

      Computes brine density as a function of temperature, pressure, and salinity using the Rowe-Chou (1970) correlation for NaCl-equivalent brine, extended with pressure correction. Fall-back is pure water density from Kell (1975). Much more accurate than the inherited hard-coded 997 kg/m3.

      Specified by:
      getDensity in interface PhaseInterface
      Overrides:
      getDensity in class PhaseGE
      Returns:
      density with unit kg/m3

    • auditNeutralPitzerParameterCoverage

      public PitzerNeutralParameterCoverage auditNeutralPitzerParameterCoverage()
      Audits neutral Pitzer families against the active opt-in topology.

      Once any neutral family is configured, lambda is required for every active neutral-neutral pair (with repetition) and neutral-ion pair, and zeta for every active neutral-cation-anion tuple. Mu and eta are audited across their active topology only when that higher-order family is present in the selected dataset. An explicitly defined zero counts as a definition.

      Returns:
      immutable coverage diagnostic

      private void ensureOwnedParameterStorage()

      Read-only clones share the large psi tensor without copying. The first parameter mutation creates independent matrices and a tensor, preserving clone independence without charging ordinary flash clones.
